createdBy: codex reviewer (session 019fcdce, T-013 plan round 1), verified and filed by claude
impact:
Found in T-013 plan review round 1 (codex session 019fcdce). This is a defect in the ticket's stated design, not in the plan written against it, which is why it is filed rather than replanned.

T-013 specifies four properties that cannot all hold:
  1. The reader lease holder computes a bounded top-up when the snapshot is stale and no service is live.
  2. Every caller is answered - fresh or honest-stale - within a bounded wait deadline.
  3. The holder computes into a PRIVATE temporary generation that is NEVER promoted and never enters the writer namespace.
  4. Measured reality (T-012's ticket, owner machine): the full ccusage pipeline is 60-80 s, and --since gives no speedup.

Take any deadline D. If D >= 60-80 s it is not a bounded client-facing wait - MCP clients time out around 60 s, which is the exact reason round 2 CUT usage_hourly. If D is small (the plan chose 4000 ms) then: a holder that waits for its own computation violates D; a holder that cancels at D means a COLD computation can never complete, so the lease never produces anything; and a holder that answers stale and detaches is, in MCP and CLI, a SHORT-LIVED PROCESS - it exits on stdio EOF or at command end and kills the only computation in flight. Because rule 3 forbids promotion, even a computation that does finish benefits nobody: the next process starts from nothing. The lease can therefore do useful work only in the narrow case where a nearly-finished holder publishes within D, and can never do the cold work it exists to do.

The herd test (AC 6) hides this rather than catching it: N clients against a stale snapshot produce exactly one computation and every caller is answered - which the design satisfies by having that one computation be killed or abandoned and everyone served honest-stale. The test passes; the feature does nothing.

THE THREE COHERENT RESOLUTIONS, all of which are owner decisions because each changes the ticket:
(a) Let the holder wait up to the measured pipeline bound and accept that the lease serves the NEXT caller rather than the current one - which requires a durable result, contradicting rule 3.
(b) Own background computation in a persistent service - that is T-011, currently parked.
(c) Permit an atomic PROMOTED cache result under a properly shared writer authority - also T-011's authority, and it makes the lease a correctness boundary rather than the optimization the ticket says it is.

Related structural findings from the same review, recorded here because they share the root cause that the reader side was scoped as if the writer side existed:
- T-010 exposes no readGeneration(id) API. readSnapshot always follows the CURRENT manifest, so a cursor cannot retrieve the generation it pinned after a publish (AC 4), and paging silently walks the new active generation instead.
- Cursor retention via createPin requires a LatchingWriteAuthority and writes through the writer's staging/pins namespace. A reader lease in its own purpose namespace cannot hold that authority, and with T-011 parked no GC runs, so pins would accumulate unbounded.
- The T-008 primitive has no production implementation at all: src/service and src/mcp do not exist and spikes/locking is explicitly evidence, not a library. Any lease in T-013 must first build the entire coordination stack T-011 was going to build - runtime directory, token, write-once allocation, identity protocol, fs adapter as sole native-error inspector.
- The lease's private computed generation must carry Provenance including ccusageFetchedAt, so the production compute path inherits ISS-075 after all; the reader-only exemption covers reading a snapshot, not computing one.
resolution:
RESOLVED 2026-08-05 as superseded by an owner-delegated design cut: the reader computation lease no longer exists in any binding document, so the four-way contradiction this issue records (bounded deadline, 60-80 s pipeline, never-promoted private result, answer-every-caller) has no home.

WHAT ANSWERED IT. N-007 decision 4 (2026-08-04, .story/notes/N-007.json): "ISS-079 / T-013 reader lease: CUT THE LEASE ENTIRELY. Readers never compute. No live service means an immediate honest-stale answer carrying freshness metadata plus an actionable service-not-running signal; cold computation belongs to the service alone... T-013 AC 6 is rewritten to this; the 60-80s measured pipeline cost makes any in-band top-up a fiction for MCP clients that time out at 60s." This is resolution (b) of the three coherent resolutions this issue itself enumerated — own background computation in a persistent service (T-011) — combined with honest-stale readers, and it was taken as an owner decision exactly as the issue said it had to be.

VERIFIED IN THE TREE, not assumed. (1) T-013's ticket text was repaired 2026-08-04 at twelve sites including the title (now "MCP server: 5 bounded snapshot tools + --cached"); its scope states "NO READER COMPUTATION — readers never compute (N-007 decision 4)... There is no lease, no lease port allocation, no `purpose` namespace, no wait deadline, no subprocess cap, no private temporary generation, and no herd contention"; AC 6 reads "CUT (N-007 decision 4). The reader computation lease and its herd test do not exist" and its replacement carries a mutant test that MUST fail if a reader-side compute path reappears — so the herd test this issue showed to be vacuous is gone, replaced by one that asserts absence of computation rather than hiding it; Scope-out forbids "any reader-side computation, in any form... not to be reintroduced as an optimization"; former open question 2 (deadline + subprocess cap) is voided. Grep of T-013 for lease/deadline/4000/herd hits only these negations and the repair log. (2) The live plan, docs/t013-replan-n007-n008-rev3.md, withdraws every lease section of the base plan (§2 map: "Base §1..., §2 Q2 (4000 ms, cap 1), §4 (the lease), §7's AC 6 row, §10.1 — all withdrawn") and states "The lease is deleted: its module, allocation and `purpose`, domain-separation tests, herd test, kill-the-holder test, private-temporary-generation rule, the 4000 ms deadline and the subprocess cap." (3) No current AC reintroduces the deadline-vs-cost tension under another name: AC 6's replacement is an IMMEDIATE honest-stale answer for N ≥ 10 concurrent clients with no computation started; AC 7's --cached "spawns no ccusage subprocess"; no AC carries a wait deadline. (4) T-011, the sole owner of cold computation, was UNPARKED 2026-08-05 (ticket open, park discharged; docs/t013-mcp-server-plan.md:3 banner; commit df2c846), so the chosen resolution routes through a live ticket.

THE RELATED STRUCTURAL FINDINGS filed here also moved. "T-010 exposes no readGeneration(id)" is no longer true: readGeneration exists at src/snapshot/store.ts:2806 (commit 9524902, ticket T-026, per N-007 decision 5). The provenance concern resolved by rename: ccusageInvokedAt is declared at src/snapshot/types.ts:301 (N-007 decision 2; ISS-077 resolved 2026-08-05), and with readers never computing, the compute-path Provenance obligation belongs to T-011's writer alone. Pin validation remains open as ISS-083 (createPin still accepts any generationId), owned there. src/service and src/mcp still do not exist — but building them is now T-011's and T-013's authorized work, not a prerequisite a lease would have had to smuggle in.

RESIDUALS, each owned by a live record: the honest-stale replacement's service-status signal is HELD on T-011's probe pending ratification (ISS-086, reopened — a reader may only report `undetermined`); T-013 itself remains parked on unrelated grounds (ISS-089/ISS-088/ISS-074/ISS-086 and T-025's park). One housekeeping residual from this closure's verification: docs/t013-mcp-server-plan.md (revision 1, REJECTED per rev3's header) still carries the lease as unmarked text — title, §1:125-136 EACCES/EADDRINUSE-collapse argument, §2 Q2:150-158 (4000 ms, cap 1), §4, the AC 6 herd row — and its 2026-08-05 banner covers only T-011's unpark; the withdrawal of those sections is recorded only in rev3's §2 map. A one-line pointer in that banner ("lease sections withdrawn per N-007 #4; see rev3 §2") would close the gap; the sections themselves stay, because superseded reasoning is preserved in this ledger, not erased.

Cross-reference: ISS-080 is the same contradiction filed from the impact side by the reviewer lane; it closes with this issue on the same evidence.

title: T-013's reader computation lease is not implementable as specified: its deadline, the measured pipeline cost, and the never-promoted rule cannot coexist
